Adolf ("Adi") and Rudolf Dassler registered the "Gebrüder Dassler Schuhfabrik" (Dassler Brothers Shoe Factory) in Herzogenaurach in 1924, after starting out making shoes in their mother's laundry room. Auf dem Gelände des Königshofes auf einer Anhöhe über der Aurach gab es bereits im 11. Audio guide · About one minute Preparing your audio guide… The audio guide could not be loaded, please retry. Sign in to listen to the audio guide
St. Magdalena is a parish church in Herzogenaurach with Gothic architecture and Baroque furnishings, standing on a hill north of the main street. A prominent bell tower at the west gable marks the exterior and is visible from a distance.
A chapel stood on the hill above the Aurach in the 11th century, dedicated to St Martin of Tours; from 1300 it was placed under Mary Magdalene. The choir is the oldest part of the Gothic church, the nave was begun around 1320 and finished in High Gothic form around 1400, closed by the slender west tower. Until the 15th century the church lay outside the town wall, sharing a walled precinct with the castle and the later episcopal office building.
The ceiling paintings and artistic stars show the region's religious craftsmanship and shape the interior space today. The four historic bells, including one from 1425 inscribed with the Evangelists' names, stand as silent witnesses to this tradition.
The church stands on a hill above the Hauptstraße, surrounded by the Kirchenplatz, which is part of the pedestrian zone; the Marienkapelle, the parish office and the town museum are on the same square. The west gable tower faces the square, and the choir lies at the east end. The nave is entered from the rear under the organ gallery.
The organ was built in 2002 by the Swiss firm Metzler, with 42 stops on three manuals and pedal and mechanical action. Donations from the local Schaeffler company paid for it. The four bells in the tower include the largest, cast in 1425 and bearing the names of the four Evangelists; the Marienglocke dates from 1651.

### The Architectural Marvel

Perched on a hillside, St. Otto’s Church is a striking landmark visible from afar. Its octagonal structure is topped with a dome crowned by a gleaming golden cross, creating a harmonious blend of traditional symbolism and contemporary design. The church’s most distinctive feature is its futuristic bell tower, an open steel framework supporting a cube-shaped belfry. This avant-garde design, connected to the main building by a glass-covered walkway, is a marvel of modern engineering and artistry.

### A Journey Through History

The story of St. Otto’s Church begins in the late 1960s, a time of growth and change in Herzogenaurach. As the population expanded, the existing St. Magdalena Church could no longer accommodate the growing Catholic community. The decision was made to establish a new parish, dedicated to Otto of Bamberg, the patron saint of the diocese. In 1974, the groundwork was laid with the construction of a kindergarten, followed by a temporary wooden church in 1979.

It wasn’t until 1987 that the Archdiocese of Bamberg granted permission for the new church building.
